system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Literature search is not available in this session: judge novelty and mechanism from the data and your reasoning.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 15 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Patient population of interest: cancers with biomarker MUT_G01240 (damaging mutation in gene G01240).

Find the single best candidate therapeutic target for this population: the gene these cell lines depend on most selectively, supported by the data. Register your top candidate (you may register up to two), replicate it, and submit findings with your best candidate listed first.

G11064's effect is mostly driven by the lung lines, with a weaker within-lung difference, and the signal sits mainly in NSCLC. The selectivity still looks real there, while the other candidates are weaker. Effect is strongest in lung (NSCLC) lines, the majority of altered lines.

output: Registered H1: MUT_G01240 -> more dependent on G11064. Discovery evidence frozen: t=-5.58, n_altered=14. Replication budget left: 5. Replication passes only if one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens.

findings.claim: Lines with damaging MUT_G01240 are more dependent on G11064 (lineage-adjusted beta -0.43; replicated in held-out Broad lines p=2.7e-4 and independent Sanger screens p=3.6e-4). Effect is concentrated in lung/NSCLC lines (9 of 14 discovery altered lines), so selectivity is strongest in that setting; the discovery signal is small (n=14 altered, 4 per replication set).

input.summary: Best candidate: G11064, the top selective dependency for MUT_G01240-mutant cancers. It passed the lineage-adjusted discovery scan (q=0.0006, 9/14 altered lines strongly dependent vs 88/612 others) and replicated in both held-out Broad lines and independent Sanger screens (one-sided p < 0.001 in each). Caveats: only 14 discovery lines carry the mutation, the signal is driven largely by lung cancer lines (leaving out lung removes most of the difference), the target is not broadly essential, and mechanism is inferred from the data rather than established. Novelty judged as not found in literature, though literature search was unavailable to check. Second-tier hits G07623 (co-associated with the same lung lines) and G05293 (broadly essential, so no therapeutic window) were not registered.
